title: Restore slot-claim envelope size cap dropped by strict-reader rewrite (regression vs main)
description: decode_cose in python/src/lichen/gateway/slot_claim.py (beads-worker-3, HEAD 2dbfec5e4d) has no envelope size cap. main's 0dba8aba95 added MAX_CLAIM_ENVELOPE_BYTES=24576 + a length check at decode entry + 2 tests; that commit is NOT an ancestor of HEAD. The strict-reader rewrite (33vn) still calls cbor2.loads(payload) at line 322 before the 4096-slot check at line 334, so the cap's DoS rationale (attacker declares a huge payload bstr head, forcing full CBOR materialization before rejection) is live on this branch. When beads-worker-3 merges to main, a wholesale 'ours' resolution silently drops the cap. Fix: re-apply len(envelope) > MAX_CLAIM_ENVELOPE_BYTES -> ClaimError before the first _read_head call, keep the constant, and restore the cap's two tests (oversized-envelope reject, max-legit accept).
close_reason: Already fixed on this branch by 81393b64b3 'fix(gateway): restore slot-claim envelope cap dropped by strict-reader rewrite' — the bead text predates that commit (cites HEAD 2dbfec5e4d). Verified complete against the bead's acceptance: MAX_CLAIM_ENVELOPE_BYTES=24576 restored (slot_claim.py:83), len(envelope) > cap -> ClaimError placed at slot_claim.py:314 immediately before the first _read_head call, both boundary tests restored and now boundary-discriminating (test_slot_claim_cose_vectors.py:284-297: exactly-at-cap parses past the size gate and fails downstream; one-over is size-rejected — addressing the 30dx off-by-one finding too). 107/107 slot-claim tests pass under uv venv. No code change needed; closing as done. No new codereview: the fix predates this claim and was reviewed in its own session.
